correctness.rationale: Definitions and all quantifiers agree with the source: T any finite tree with t>=2 and m>=2, N=mt; Δ_2^t(K_m square T)=Cl(K_m square T)^vee. The N-vertex equivariant complement-chain Alexander duality produces reduced H_{N-4}(Δ;Z)=H^1(Cl(G);Z) tensor det(Z^N), giving precisely sgn(row)^t sgn(tree)^m. A clique involving >=3 vertices belongs entirely to a K_m fiber because the tree has no triangles; collapsing contractible fibers yields a graph with m parallel edges over each tree edge. Its chain boundary is the row-sum ε⊗∂_T and ∂_T is injective, so H1=ker ε⊗oriented_edges(T), and H^1=(Z^m/Z·1)⊗E_T integrally; replacing by the root lattice would be incorrect. Fixed-color/edge signed trace gives the printed character. Computing symmetric row-permutation coinvariants of the quotient lattice gives Z/m for t even, sign-twisted Z for (m=2,t odd), Z/2 for (even m>=4,t odd) and zero for odd m>=3,t odd. Independently constructed 10 integer presentations, m=2..6 with and without sign, and Smith normal forms reproduced all cases. The finite checks support, but do not replace, the all-tree proof.
